**English** · [简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/README.ja.md)
# OpenMotion OpenMotion is a **full-stack agentic video** studio and an **open-source alternative to Claude Motion and CapCut**. Upload a reference video or paste a social video link to **recreate it with your own brand kit and copy**. - 🎬 **Full-stack video recreation.** Code video with HTML. Your agent breaks down the reference, rebuilds its shots and transitions, and generates missing assets. Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project. - 🔑 **BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys.** OpenMotion is free and open source. Recreate videos in [your local agent](#agent-wall) with your own API keys. Supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, and WorkBuddy. - 🧩 OpenMotion introduces **Motion.md**, a Markdown format for shot order, timing and transitions. Use it to share how a brand film works, shot by shot. - 🎛️ **Images, video, music and voice.** Create artwork with GPT Image 2.6, add a shot with Seedance 2.5, score it with Suno and narrate it with Eleven v4. [Explore the models and providers](#model-wall). ### Install from ChatGPT Marketplace **One-click installation. No manual configuration required.** Once installed, create motion videos from scratch, recreate reference videos, or start from a template—all in your conversation. **[Install OpenMotion in ChatGPT →](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6a742d13e88481919b42002864b1bb26)** ### Install in your agent Install the main Skill with the [Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): ```sh npx skills add nexu-io/openmotion --skill openmotion ``` Then ask your agent: **Use OpenMotion to install and connect the local Studio and MCP, then help me make a video.** The Skill completes the source setup below when needed and reuses an existing workspace. Installing the Skill alone copies instructions; it does not yet install Studio or connect MCP. Copy this instruction into your local agent to set up OpenMotion from source: ```text Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/docs/install.md and follow the instructions to install and connect OpenMotion in the current agent. ``` After setup, the agent opens the local template library and shows the welcome followed by three project-preview cards in a self-contained HTML document. Each installation samples three distinct entries from the curated pool of four. The complete silent previews and posters are bundled, so this display does not wait for native MCP reload or fetch remote reference films. Native original-reference playback remains available separately and requires internet access. The library opens once using the opening tool's result, with no extra page or playback audit. An opening failure is reported with a usable link and does not invalidate installation. Automatic current-chat MCP activation is assessed independently. Preview a card, choose **Recreate template**, then send your brief to start creating. [Source installation guide](docs/install.md) · [Onboarding selection](docs/install.md#maintained-recommendation-selection) ### Install the published npm app (optional) Source setup above remains the default for repository installation. To explicitly choose the published application with prebuilt Studio and its configured online catalog, copy this instruction into your local agent: ```text Read https://releases.open-design.ai/motion and follow the instructions to install and connect the published npm application in the current agent. ``` [Published application installation and channel selection](docs/install.md). Published versions can lag behind this checkout. ### Run the repository locally Use Git, npm and Node.js 26.11.1: ```sh git -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.required=false clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion.git cd openmotion npm ci npm run build:studio npm start ``` Open the actual `studioUrl` or `previewUrl` printed at startup, then choose **Template library**. Studio and MCP read the templates in this checkout. To connect your agent to this same copy, follow [source setup and MCP configuration](#agent-setup). [Clone size and optional media](docs/repository-storage.md) ### Start from an existing project Import a **HyperFrames project ZIP** into OpenMotion to continue editing its composition and local assets. Compress the project folder, open **All projects → Import projects**, then select the imported copy to edit in Studio or with your Agent. Import creates an independent copy and requires a supported native project structure. [Step-by-step import guide, required files and compatibility](docs/project-archives.md#import-from-hyperframes) **22 local agents** · [Choose your agent](#choose-agent)

## 🎞️ Use cases and remake examples Explore product demos, brand films, talking-head videos and more. HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 9. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, share, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | | `/reverse-any-video` | Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro. | | `/style-sampling` | Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? details.readme:
Your AI VTuber Studio

Give a character a personality, and in minutes it's chatting with you or streaming live. Or play it yourself.

English · 中文 · 日本語

- Up to 30 characters on one stage (15 in a browser): LivLiv half-body and full-body, VRM and PNGTuber - Long-term memory and real-time voice chat - Characters that talk to each other and to your Twitch chat - Emotional reactions as they speak - AI chat that remembers, in the desktop app: each character keeps its own memory, powered by [Project AIRI](https://github.com/moeru-ai/airi) - Game connections in the desktop app: Minecraft through [Airicraft](https://github.com/proj-airi/airicraft), Factorio through [Autorio](https://github.com/moeru-ai/airi-factorio), or any game window the character watches - Built-in Neuro SDK support (desktop app) - All the basics: webcam face tracking (phone apps and VMC/OSC in the desktop app), OBS output, video recording - 27 featured characters, ready to use. Built on [LivLiv Player](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player) The AI runs on your own model key (OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek and more), or your LivLiv.ai account. Real-time voice needs your own OpenAI or Alibaba Cloud Bailian key. ## Try it - **Desktop app**: macOS and Windows from [Releases](https://github.com/livliv-dev/stage/releases/latest). If GitHub is slow, use the [backup download](https://downloads.livliv.ai/stage/index.html). On macOS, one line in Terminal installs it with no first-open prompt: `curl -fsSL https://livliv.ai/stage/install.sh | bash` - **Online (Web, limited features)**: [livliv.ai/stage](https://livliv.ai/stage) - **From source**: see [Develop](#develop)

## Characters The featured characters have [their own licence](stage/public/characters/LICENSE.md). **Import** brings your own: a `.livliv` package from [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai), a VRM, or a PNGTuber. ## Project LivLiv We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone. We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, [the player and its playback protocol](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player), and [a stage where your characters can meet an audience](https://github.com/livliv-dev/stage). Come say hello on [Discord](https://discord.gg/ac5qF36T2H) and follow us on [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/livliv_ai). ## Develop Node.js 22.18 or later. ```sh git clone https://github.com/livliv-dev/stage cd stage npm --prefix stage ci && npm --prefix stage run dev # the web app at http://127.0.0.1:5222 npm --prefix desktop ci && npm --prefix desktop run stage:dev # the desktop app (stage:mac, stage:win build installers) ``` Tests: `npm --prefix stage run check && npm --prefix stage test`, `npm --prefix desktop test`, `npm --prefix collab test`; the browser checks are the `test:*` scripts in [stage/package.json](stage/package.json), and GitHub Actions runs all of these on every pull request. AI chat and memory: [docs/ai-conversations.md](docs/ai-conversations.md), real-time voice: [docs/realtime-voice.md](docs/realtime-voice.md), built-in AIRI ([docs/airi.md](docs/airi.md)), the Neuro SDK bridge: [neuro/README.md](neuro/README.md), the local control API: [docs/stage-api.md](docs/stage-api.md), co-streaming: [collab/README.md](collab/README.md). Model keys stay in the browser or the app and go straight to the provider. Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License Stage's code is under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). The bundled [AIRI core](vendor/airi-core/LICENSE) and its [dependencies](vendor/airi-core/DEPENDENCY-NOTICES.txt) carry their own licenses. The featured characters have [their own licence](stage/public/characters/LICENSE.md). You may keep the LivLiv name and logo in your own versions, as long as they don't claim to be the official one: [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).

details.readme:
SharkyClips

Your stream in, ready-to-post Shorts out. Free, and 100% on your own PC.

SharkyClips watches your Twitch, YouTube or Kick VOD (or any video file) the way an editor would: it hears the hype, reads the chat replay and the game's HUD, cuts the best moments, bleeps the swears, writes the titles and posts 9:16 clips to YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels. No account, no cloud, no credits, no watermark.
Formerly ClipForge: old links redirect, and your settings move over by themselves.

Windows 10 / 11, 64-bit · 8 GB RAM · no GPU needed · install steps

Install · Highlights · How it works · All features · FAQ · Technical guide · Türkçe

## Highlights
🔒 Free & local
Whisper, the language model, highlight detection and rendering run on your GPU or CPU. MIT-licensed, no subscription, no telemetry. Nothing leaves your PC unless you press Publish.		 🎮 Game-aware clips
Loudness, laughter, reaction words, chat explosions and, for Delta Force and League of Legends, the HUD itself: kills, multikills, objectives. A pentakill is never cut in half.		 🤐 Swears bleeped, checked
Swears in 11 languages are bleeped or muted, and every rendered clip is listened to again. A clip with an audible swear is held back instead of posted.
📤 One Publish, three platforms
YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels from one button: per-platform captions and limits, planned times, retries, views coming back. TikTok's required post screen is built in.		 🌍 11 languages
Interface, speech recognition, titles and subtitles in English, Türkçe, Español, Português (Brasil), Русский, Deutsch, Français, العربية (right-to-left), 中文, 日本語 and Magyar. Titles can be in another language than the one spoken.		 🦈 Stays out of your way
Silent mode pauses while you play or watch fullscreen and gives the game its VRAM back. Easy mode does everything by itself; Pro mode gives you every knob.
## See it in action Review a candidate, accept it, render. The clips land in the Clips tab, ready to download. ![Demo: selecting clip candidates, accepting two of them and rendering them as 9:16 clips](docs/demo.gif)

Library: every stream with live progress
Clips: rendered 9:16 clips, playable and downloadable

Best-of video: 16:9 compilation with chapters
Settings: language, performance mode, accounts, local AI
More screenshots, in both themes, are in [docs/screenshots](docs/screenshots). ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph IN[Input] A1[Twitch / YouTube / Kick link] A2[Video file or OBS folder] end subgraph LOCAL[Your PC: Python backend] B[Ingest
yt-dlp · FFmpeg] C[Transcribe
faster-whisper · mlx-whisper] D[Chat replay
Twitch · YouTube · Kick] E[Signals
loudness · laughter · keywords
speech · game HUD · chat] F[Hype Map
rank · snap to words · shape] G[Local LLM via Ollama
score · titles · descriptions] H[Render 9:16
FFmpeg · captions · bleeps · zoom] I[Bleep check
re-listen every clip] end subgraph OUT[Output] J[MP4 / MOV / GIF
SRT · FCPXML · Premiere XML] K[YouTube · TikTok · Reels
official APIs] end A1 --> B A2 --> B B --> C --> E B --> D --> E E --> F --> G --> H --> I I --> J I --> K ``` The web UI (React) talks to a local FastAPI server on `127.0.0.1`. A persistent job queue runs the heavy steps in lanes (GPU, CPU, I/O, network), and a resource governor decides how fast they may run from what you're doing (game in front, fullscreen video, away from the PC). Whisper and the language model never share the GPU. Every step caches its result, so a closed app resumes where it stopped. Details: **[docs/how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md)**. ## Tech stack | Layer | Built with | |---|---| | UI | React 18, TypeScript, Vite; 7 locales with a completeness check in CI; dark and light themes; axe-checked accessibility | | Server | Python 3.11-3.13, FastAPI + Uvicorn, a persistent multi-lane job queue, a resource governor (psutil, NVML) | | Speech | faster-whisper (CUDA / CPU), mlx-whisper (Apple Silicon), a CTC aligner for word timing, sherpa-onnx (laughter, voices) | | Analysis | NumPy / SciPy signal scoring, librosa (music mode), OpenCV (facecam), RapidOCR (game HUD) | | Language model | Ollama with Qwen 3.5 (4B / 9B, picked from your VRAM), structured JSON output | | Video | FFmpeg filter graphs, NVENC / VideoToolbox / QSV / AMF hardware encoding, yt-dlp | | Publishing | YouTube Data + Analytics APIs (OAuth + PKCE), TikTok Content Posting API, Instagram Graph API; tokens encrypted with DPAPI / Keychain | | Quality | 600+ pytest tests on Windows, Ubuntu and macOS; ruff; a Playwright layout check at 9 screen sizes (phone to 1920 px) in 3 languages and both themes; a pixel check that the live preview matches the render | | Install | One-click PowerShell (Windows) and shell (macOS) installers, in-app updates via git | ## All features
Everything SharkyClips does (click to open) - **Easy mode (the default).** Drop a video or paste a link: SharkyClips picks the best clips, shapes them (smart cuts, length and pacing for Shorts, a hook check with a banner), renders them and shows them as a grid with one Publish button each. Autopilot can even post them on a schedule and send you a morning summary. Pro mode keeps every setting below. - **Swear check after every render.** Each rendered clip is listened to again; a swear that is still audible is bleeped wider and re-rendered, and if it still can't be fixed the clip is held back from automatic uploads until you listen to it. - **One Publish for YouTube, TikTok and Instagram Reels.** Per-platform captions with the limits checked (and one-tap fixes), planned times, retries with backoff, crash-safe resumable posts, and views flowing back from every platform. TikTok's required post screen (privacy, interactions, content disclosure) is built in. - **Finds the moments worth posting.** Volume spikes, laughter and shouting, reaction words ("NO WAY", "allah allah", "KEKW"), fast talk, chat explosions from the chat replay and, in study mode, self-contained explanations. All of it goes into one **Hype Map** with ranked clip candidates. - **Knows the game.** For **Delta Force** and **League of Legends** it reads the game's HUD: kills, multikills (pentakill >> double kill), first blood, objectives, own deaths, victory/defeat and extraction screens, in English and Turkish clients. Clips always contain the whole multikill, and the AI writes titles from these events ("Quadra kill with Teemo"). The game is recognized from the title or what's said, or picked per project; a **Game detection** page shows what was read, so the HUD boxes can be fixed after a game update. Optional: your own short sound clips (announcer lines) are found in the audio. - **Cuts that make sense.** Clip edges snap to word boundaries (never mid-word), and the local AI can move them a few seconds to include the setup or the payoff. - **A viral score and titles that sound like you.** A local language model rates every clip (hook, retention, trend fit), writes titles, a **YouTube description** (2-3 sentences + hashtags), hashtags, a hook text and a cover prompt, each with a copy button. Thumbs up/down teach it your style; a glossary keeps names spelled right. - **Ready-to-post 9:16 clips.** Facecam on top and gameplay below (detected automatically and adjustable), burned-in word-timed subtitles (also right-to-left Arabic), an optional hook text and a "peak flash" opener. Encodes on NVIDIA, Apple, Intel or AMD hardware when available. - **Editing tools.** Swear words bleeped or muted (11 languages, editable lists, "a**" in the captions; on by default for Shorts-style videos), silences and filler words ("um", "ııı", "äh"...) cut with tiny crossfades but never inside a laugh, a subtle smart zoom on the peak moments and on your facecam when you react, and **edit by transcript**: delete words to cut them, drag the first and last word to trim, with undo and a live preview. - **Your own music and brand.** Drop your songs (e.g. your AI songs) into the music library and tag their mood; SharkyClips suggests a fitting one per clip, starts it at its strongest part, ducks it under your voice and keeps the mix at -14 LUFS, with an optional credit line for YouTube. A brand kit adds your logo watermark, @handle, intro/outro cards and caption style with one switch. - **Fast review.** Keyboard shortcuts for everything (A keep, X skip, J/K/L, I/O to mark your own clip...) and a full-screen, swipe-style review of one clip at a time. - **Export for every platform.** MP4 (H.264, HEVC, AV1 on recent GPUs), MOV, WebM, GIF with a size limit, MP3/M4A. One-click presets for **YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels, X and YouTube 16:9** set size, fps, bitrate and length limit and keep subtitles out of each app's buttons. # Jev Cookbook **100 notebook recipes for typed decisions with Jev, covering text and images, starting from a first `Choice` question.** ![Recipes: 56 of 100 published](https://img.shields.io/badge/Recipes-56%20of%20100%20published-F386A1?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![Status: in progress](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-in%20progress-E551BA?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![Categories: 15](https://img.shields.io/badge/Categories-15-F386A1?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![Levels: 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/Levels-5-F386A1?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![Python: 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.10%2B-F386A1?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-DEDEDE?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E)](LICENSE) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How a recipe works](#how-a-recipe-works) · [Decision types](#decision-types) · [Levels](#difficulty-levels) · [Categories](#browse-by-category) · [Recipes](#the-recipes) · [Sources](#sources) · [Contributing](#contributing)
--- Jev is TypeSafe AI's System One model. It does not write text. You send it a **state** and a set of **typed questions**, and it returns structured answers your code can branch on, sort by, and route with. This cookbook is a curriculum of Jupyter notebooks that teach that way of building, one bounded decision at a time. > [!NOTE] > **The generated badge and recipes table show what has shipped.** The catalog lists the planned use cases, categories, and difficulty levels, and it can be revised as recipes are built. A recipe counts as published once its `notebook.ipynb` is in the repository, and its row then links to the notebook. Every other row is marked coming soon. It links to the issue tracking the recipe when the catalog records one; a row for an entry with no issue yet is marked coming soon with no link. Each published recipe states in its notebook and README which mode it ran in (synthetic fixtures or recorded responses), and for recorded responses the model version the API returned and the date. Metrics from synthetic runs check that the pipeline behaves as designed. They are not Jev results. Any number reported as a Jev result states the number of examples it was measured on and the model version, comes from recorded inference on a held-out set, and makes no general claim about Jev's quality, latency, or cost. Where a recipe has no such run, its README says "not measured live". ## Quick start You need Python 3.10 or newer and git. No API key is needed to run anything offline. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook.git cd cookbook python -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate # Git Bash: source .venv/Scripts/activate; PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 pip install -e ".[dev]" python tools/execute_notebook.py recipes/_template # run the template notebook offline ``` The template in `recipes/_template/` is a small, complete recipe, and every recipe works the same way; recipe 01 is the start of the curriculum once its row below links to a notebook. These pages take it from here: - [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, open a notebook, run it offline, run a recipe's tests, switch to live. - [Offline and live](docs/offline-and-live.md): what each mode is, what provenance says, why synthetic metrics are pipeline checks, and what "not measured live" means. - [Glossary](docs/glossary.md): state, question, `Choice`, `Noul`, `Score`, criteria, probabilities, confidence, threshold, replay key, fixture, provenance, and run mode, each linked to its source. - [Images, boxes and ordered frames](docs/vision.md): the local helpers in `jev_cookbook.vision` for image assets, Box coordinates, tiles and loading timestamped frames, and in `jev_cookbook.frames` for sampling and windowing them. - [Multimodal track](docs/multimodal-track.md): the forty planned recipes 61–100, what must hold before one is ready, and what its evaluation must show. ## How a recipe works Each notebook keeps the same division of labour. Jev supplies a narrow semantic judgment. Python does everything exact: arithmetic, retrieval, policy, permissions, and execution. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#E551BA'}}}%% flowchart LR F["Prepared fixtures
text or JSON"]:::panel --> Q["Typed questions
Choice · Noul · Score"]:::pink Q --> J["Jev
one focused judgment each"]:::ink J --> A["Typed answers
with probabilities"]:::pink A --> P["Your Python
policy, arithmetic, execution"]:::panel P --> E["Evaluation
labels, baselines, held-out sets"]:::ink classDef ink fill:#1E1E1E,stroke:#F386A1,color:#FEFEFE classDef pink fill:#F386A1,stroke:#1E1E1E,color:#1E1E1E classDef panel fill:#DEDEDE,stroke:#1E1E1E,color:#1E1E1E ``` A question is a few lines of Python. This is the shape recipe 01 starts from, using the TypeSafe Python SDK: ```python from typesafe_sdk import Choice, TypeSafeClient with TypeSafeClient() as client: # reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY response = client.system_one( state={"review": "Arrived fast, but the lid cracked within a week."}, questions={ "sentiment": Choice( instructions="What is the overall sentiment of this review?", criteria={"positive": None, "neutral": None, "negative": None, "mixed": None}, ), }, ) print(response.choices["sentiment"].choice) ``` What every recipe assumes: | | | | --- | --- | | **You** | Know basic Python. No machine learning background is needed for levels 1 to 3. | | **Data** | Prepared text or JSON fixtures that ship with the recipe. The inputs are written for the recipe, never real data. Stored answers are synthetic unless the recipe says they were recorded from real calls, with the model and the date. | | **Actions** | Simulated. No recipe sends a message, moves a file, or touches a real system. | | **Model calls** | Offline by default, replaying fixtures. Live Jev calls are opt-in with your own key. | | **Claims** | Runs on synthetic or scripted answers show that the pipeline works. Statements about quality, latency, or cost need recorded inference on a held-out set, with the model version, the capture date and the number of examples (N), and a recipe says which one you are looking at. | ## Decision types The catalog uses Jev's own vocabulary. Every recipe is tagged with the primitives it asks for. | Type | Role | How to read it | | --- | --- | --- | | `Choice` | Select one option | Select one item from supplied alternatives, including none, other, or uncertain outcomes when the task needs them. Returns the choice, a probability per option, and a confidence. | | `Noul` | Judge a proposition | Return the probability that a stated proposition holds. Tasks that allow several labels ask one independent question per label. There is no separate confidence field. | | `Score` | Evaluate a rubric | Return a position and a distribution over ordered rubric levels you define. Exact measurements and arithmetic stay in code. | | `Box` | Locate one target | Return one bounding rectangle for one target, with four edges as fractions of the image's width and height and a confidence. It is never a mask and never a set of detections, and it always returns a rectangle, even when the target is absent, so check presence separately, for example with a paired `Noul`. Requires the Jev 1.14 preview and the experimental images header. | | Combination | Compose judgments | Combine independent questions in Python, and make a later request when one judgment depends on an earlier answer. | A single label can stand for several independent questions of that type. Thresholds are a property of the task, so each recipe that uses one chooses it from examples and evaluates it. ## Difficulty levels In the original track (ranks 1 to 60) the levels rise with rank: rank 1 is the easiest recipe and rank 60 the most demanding, so follow those ranks for a full learning sequence. The multimodal track (ranks 61 to 100) is ordered by category block, not by difficulty, so its levels rise and fall as the rank increases; use each recipe's level, or pick a category, to choose a path through it. | Level | Name | What a notebook at this level involves | Recipes | | :---: | --- | --- | :---: | | **1** | [Beginner](#level-1--beginner) | One bounded judgment over a short prepared input with direct inspection of typed results. | 11
01 to 10, 61 | | **2** | [Easy](#level-2--easy) | Context-sensitive matching, scoring, or verification with candidate sets and explicit uncertain or no-match outcomes. | 24
11 to 23, 66, 69 to 76, 85 to 86 | | **3** | [Intermediate](#level-3--intermediate) | Multiple judgments or stages, structured evidence, deterministic composition, and task-level evaluation. | 34
24 to 39, 62 to 65, 67 to 68, 77 to 79, 81 to 82, 87 to 93 | | **4** | [Advanced](#level-4--advanced) | Stateful workflows, provenance, adversarial cases, model calibration, or several integrated decision stages. | 22
40 to 52, 80, 83 to 84, 94 to 97, 99 to 100 | | **5** | [Expert](#level-5--expert) | Controlled optimization studies or closed-loop simulations requiring budgets, baselines, and held-out or trajectory evaluation. | 9
53 to 60, 98 | Ranks are editorial estimates of implementation and evaluation effort. Neighbouring recipes are ordered for learning, not by a measured difference in difficulty. ## Browse by category | Category | Recipes | Levels | Recipe numbers | | --- | :---: | :---: | --- | | **Data quality & knowledge graphs** | 9 | 2 to 5 | `14` `22` `33` `34` `37` `39` `40` `47` `57` | | **Agent orchestration** | 8 | 2 to 4 | `11` `27` `28` `29` `43` `44` `49` `51` | | **Bounding boxes & spatial reasoning** | 8 | 3 to 4 | `77` `78` `79` `80` `81` `82` `83` `84` | | **Image understanding & visual judgments** | 8 | 1 to 3 | `61` `62` `63` `64` `65` `66` `67` `68` | | **Language & content** | 8 | 1 to 2, 4 | `01` `03` `05` `06` `07` `12` `13` `48` | | **Multiframe & temporal understanding** | 8 | 2 to 3 | `85` `86` `87` `88` `89` `90` `91` `92` | | **Multimodal & long context** | 8 | 3 to 5 | `93` `94` `95` `96` `97` `98` `99` `100` | | **Visual criteria & reference matching** | 8 | 2 | `69` `70` `71` `72` `73` `74` `75` `76` | | **Evaluation & optimization** | 7 | 2 to 5 | `23` `35` `38` `50` `53` `54` `55` | | **Search & retrieval** | 6 | 1 to 4 | `08` `10` `17` `20` `30` `52` | | **Trust & security** | 6 | 2 to 5 | `15` `16` `26` `41` `42` `56` | | **Workflow & service operations** | 6 | 1 to 3 | `02` `04` `09` `18` `24` `25` | | **Games & simulation** | 5 | 2 to 3, 5 | `21` `36` `58` `59` `60` | | **Software engineering** | 3 | 2 to 3 | `19` `31` `32` | | **Memory & context** | 2 | 4 | `45` `46` | ## The recipes ### Original track (01–60) Text and structured-state decisions using Choice, Noul, and Score, from single judgments to evaluated workflows and simulations. #### Level 1 · Beginner One bounded judgment over a short prepared input with direct inspection of typed results. | # | Recipe | Category | Decision | Status | | :---:

[![YuE2 Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/YuE2_Studio-songs_with_a_score-ec4899?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/timoncool/YuE2-Studio) [![MiniMax Music3 Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/MiniMax_Music3_Studio-full--length_tracks-3f3f46?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/timoncool/MiniMax-Music3-Studio) [![ACE-Step Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/ACE--Step_Studio-Suno_at_home-3f3f46?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/timoncool/ACE-Step-Studio) # YuE2 Studio **Full songs with an editable score, generated on your own GPU. One executable — no Python, no Node.js, no launcher.** [![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project_page-timoncool.github.io-7c3aed?style=for-the-badge)](https://timoncool.github.io/YuE2-Studio/) [![Download](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-Windows_x64-0078D6?style=for-the-badge&logo=windows&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/timoncool/YuE2-Studio/releases/latest) [![Donate](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support-Donate-ff69b4?style=for-the-badge)](DONATE.md) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/timoncool/YuE2-Studio?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/timoncool/YuE2-Studio?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/YuE2-Studio/stargazers) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/timoncool/YuE2-Studio?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/YuE2-Studio/commits/main) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/timoncool/YuE2-Studio/total?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/timoncool/YuE2-Studio/releases) **English** · [Русский](https://timoncool.github.io/YuE2-Studio/ru.html) · [中文](https://timoncool.github.io/YuE2-Studio/zh.html) · [日本語](https://timoncool.github.io/YuE2-Studio/ja.html) · [한국어](https://timoncool.github.io/YuE2-Studio/ko.html) · [Português](https://timoncool.github.io/YuE2-Studio/pt.html) ![YuE2 Studio](docs/screenshots/en-01-create.png)
YuE2 Studio is a desktop studio for **YuE2**, the open song model from M-A-P that writes a score before it sings. Describe a style, write the lyrics, and the model composes a melody with chords as sheet music, then performs it as a full song with vocals. The score comes back with the track: read it, edit it, and render the same composition again with a different sound. Windows installer with auto-update or a portable folder, runs offline on an NVIDIA card with 6 GB of VRAM or more; AMD and Intel cards through Vulkan are experimental. It is built on [yue2.cpp](https://github.com/ServeurpersoCom/yue2.cpp), the native C++/CUDA port of YuE2. The studio around it is Rust and React in a Tauri window — nothing in the runtime path is Python. ## For AI agents Given this repository, an agent can set everything up and drive the studio by itself: 1. Install the studio from the [latest release](https://github.com/timoncool/YuE2-Studio/releases/latest) and start it, with `--headless` to keep its window off the user's screen (see [Drive it from an agent](#drive-it-from-an-agent-mcp)). 2. Connect to its MCP server at `http://127.0.0.1:8791/mcp`: `claude mcp add --transport http yue2-studio http://127.0.0.1:8791/mcp` 3. Read the skill it serves (resource `studio://skill`, prompt `studio`), the same text as [docs/mcp-skill.md](docs/mcp-skill.md), and start with the tool `studio_status`. [llms.txt](llms.txt) says the same for tools that look for it. To keep the skill in Claude Code, save [docs/mcp-skill.md](docs/mcp-skill.md) as `~/.claude/skills/yue2-studio/SKILL.md`. ## What you can do - **A player of its own** — a ten-band equalizer on Winamp's frequencies with its presets, your own and .EQF files; a MilkDrop visualiser with hundreds of presets, a spectrum in ten looks, a black hole with its disk of light that brightens and tilts with the song, or a flight through a tunnel that jumps on the loud notes, over the studio, fullscreen or in its own window; and a Winamp mode that turns the whole window into a skinned Winamp 2 whose windows move apart, dock and resize — the original skin and ten more included, sharp at any scale, the Winamp Skin Museum one click away, Ctrl+M to switch. The song, its place and the equalizer carry over both ways. - **Save as, and a Files panel** — songs, stems, MIDI, lyric sheets, scores and videos are saved where you say, in Windows' own Save dialog, and the Files panel shows each save. - **A proxy for the whole studio** — HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 or SOCKS4, with a login: model downloads, Hugging Face, OpenRouter and updates go through it. - **Models on another disk** — the setup screen and Settings show where the downloads are kept and how much room that disk has; one button moves the model sets, LoRAs, the stem separator, karaoke, the assistant's models, the trainer and Audio to MIDI to another folder, leaving a link so everything that shares them keeps working. Songs and datasets stay. One more button brings them back. - **Full songs from a style and lyrics** — up to ten minutes, in the languages the model sings. In Russian a stress mark (the combining acute U+0301, Alt+0769 on Windows) after a vowel moves the sung stress to it, as Ruach Studio documents. On an RTX 4090 with the Q8_0 set a 3:38 song renders in about 46 seconds. - **Songs one by one** — ask for several songs at once and each lands in the library as soon as it is finished, ready to play while the rest are still made; a stopped request keeps the songs it finished. - **Read and edit the score** — the model writes its composition in ABC notation first; the studio engraves it as sheet music. Edit the notes, tempo or key and create again: the composition stays, the performance changes. Or switch to melody-only, or no score at all. - **Compose the score first** — write only the score from the style and lyrics, without singing it (the studio's take on yue2.cpp's `yue-plan`), read and fix it, then create. - **Covers** — SheetSage2 listens to a recording and writes its melody as a score; YuE2 then sings that melody in your style. The words have to fit the melody: the original lyrics work best, new ones need the same syllables line by line with the stresses on the same notes, or the singing drifts off the tune — lines stretch, pause and slide into the wrong section. Transcription mistakes carry into the cover too. A track from your library can be transcribed from its menu. - **Exact replay** — every track keeps its request and its audio codes, so it can be re-rendered bit for bit, or re-rendered with other steps, a new sound seed, several variations, or another output format, without composing again. - **110 ready examples** — the style/lyrics/score sets that ship with yue2.cpp, covers included, one click to load. - **Every engine setting** — all seven sampling knobs (temperature, top-p, top-k, repetition penalty and its window, minimum and maximum tokens) for the score and for the audio codes, flow-matching steps, guidance, both seeds, lossless FLAC or MP3. Prompts open and save as JSON or YAML in the engine's own request format, so they move freely between the studio, the yue2.cpp WebUI and `yue-synth`. - **Structured song writing** — build a style from its musical fields and arrange lyrics in editable sections, while keeping the plain text editable. Give the writing assistant a language, a target of 8–32 lines and additional instructions. - **Song and render controls** — voice and tempo fields; section, line/stanza and text-case tools; Keep/Words lyric preservation and exact checkpoint tokens; batch score-plan selection and chord mirroring in repeated sections. Edit scores with MIDI grid and octave controls. Transpose generation by −24 to +24 semitones, render vocals only through native HT-Demucs as MP3 or 32-bit WAV, and switch each LoRA on or off with weights from −10 to +10. - **A writing assistant** — a local Gemma model or OpenRouter writes the style and lyrics from an idea and edits the score on request; or pick your connected agent (MCP) and it writes instead. Lyrics you wrote yourself get their section tags with one button, the words exactly as you wrote them. - **Word-level karaoke** — enhanced LRC with a timestamp on every word, aligned by Parakeet or Whisper. Your lyrics are kept; only the timing is borrowed. - **Six stems on the GPU** — drums, bass, other, vocals, guitar and piano with HT-Demucs. - **A stem mixer** — a song's stems play together on one transport over its waveform, each with mute, solo, volume and pan, and a loop over a section: the drums with the bass alone, or the band without the voice. The stem files stay as separated. - **Any track to MIDI** — a song, a stem or a processed take becomes multi-instrument MIDI (34 instrument groups and drums) with MuScriptor on the GPU, in the audio.cpp server. A piano roll fills in while it listens; play it against the original, mute or solo an instrument, save the .mid. Downloaded the first time it is used. - **Restore a track after compression** — Apollo removes the artefacts of MP3 compression from a song or any audio file and gives 44.1 kHz in the source's channels, as a new track beside it, in the audio.cpp server. - **A MIDI editor** — a piano roll with tracks, instruments and drums: play a song in from a MIDI keyboard or the computer's keys, record or draw it, edit a track's MIDI, save it to the library as a track and send it to a cover, or open the create form's score in it. A .mid file becomes the score: the voice and instrument chosen, chords read or guessed, karaoke words offered for the lyrics. - **Every result is a track** — stems, a processed take, a re-render and a cover land in the library as tracks of their own, each marked with the one it was made from and keeping the settings it was made with. - **LoRA** — LoRA and LoKr files for either half of the model, the composition or the sound, each with its own strength, picked in the create form. A catalogue of ready ones with their authors credited, and a search on Hugging Face that downloads what you pick. - **Ruach Studio's sound in one step** — the "Ruach Studio" preset in Settings - Models puts their fine-tune in place of the set's model and their YuE2-VAE-RS x3 decoder in place of the VAE's own, and downloads what is missing; the decoder alone can be chosen on any set. It keeps the 10-16 kHz band at the source's level and adds nothing above 20 kHz, at 4 GB of the card while it decodes against 2.5 GB. Six more community models - Ruach Studio's IRA and IRAE merges - are in the list of your own models, in Q8_0 and Q6_K. - **Train your own LoRA** — an optional tab on the LoRA page: songs of one artist or style become a LoRA on your own card with HOT-Step's trainer and its tuned recipe (LoKr, Prodigy, lyric timing from a forced aligner that also reads Cyrillic). Every setting of the recipe is editable. Datasets move between this studio and MiniMax Music3 Studio as a folder, and each saved checkpoint goes into the LoRA library in one click. - **A three-step wizard** — drop a folder of songs, check them, train. Albums with a cue sheet are cut into songs; titles and artists come from the tags, the file name and the folders. - **Preparation on its own** — lyrics come from the lyric databases players use (LRCLIB, QQ Music, Kugou), word for word; only a song none of them knows has its vocals separated and is heard by Whisper, with its usual hallucinations filtered out. The assistant lays the lyrics out in sections. MOSS-Music listens to every song and the assistant writes its style, with the tempo measured by Beat This! on the card. - **Every song shows where it is** — the lyrics and styles appear as each song is done, one model on the card at a time, each loaded once for the whole batch. details.readme:
laya is free and open source. If it helps you, sponsor the work on GitHub.

**New in 0.5: laya reads images, audio and video, takes 73k tokens, says when it should not decide, and keeps learning.** All open source under Apache 2.0 (`pip install -U laya`). - **Text, images, audio and video.** `agent.predict(...)` with `image=`, `audio=` or `video=` gives the same typed answers as for text. - **73,728 tokens of context.** Whole contracts, threads and logs in one read. - **Abstain and unbound**, explained below. - **Physics, not text generation.** Each candidate answer is a valley; the input is a particle that rolls and settles in one. Deterministic, constant cost, nothing generated. - **Any LLM as the reader.** One small decision engine on top of a frozen reader, from 0.8B to 27B. - **Continuous learning.** `from laya import Learner`: it answers from day one and learns from every answer your team confirms, on your own machine, in seconds on a CPU with no fine-tuning. ### How abstain and unbound work The input is placed as a particle in a small decision space where every candidate answer is a valley. Where the particle settles, and how deep, is the answer and its probability. - **`abstain`**: it declines to commit. The threshold is calibrated so that, among the answers it does give, the error rate stays under the configured risk (10% by default). - **`prediction_set`**: the conformal set, every option the answer could still be at `alpha` 0.10. One option means it is sure; two or more means the input really is ambiguous. - **`unbound`**: the particle settled far from every valley, so the input looks unlike anything it knows (likely off-distribution). It is reported on every answer but does not route on its own: measured, it also fired on 71% of normal banking77 rows, so it would have sent most good answers to review. - **`route`**: what to do with it, `auto` or `review`. Without labels, `review` when it abstains or the set holds more than one option. With labels (`agent.fit` / `agent.calibrate`), a band placed where precision holds at 95% on your rows decides. Gate on `route`, never on a confidence number. ### Benchmarks at a glance **Continuous learning.** 14 decision templates (31 questions), each starting from about 600 generated examples, then learning from confirmed answers; scored on 60 held-out rows per template. | | day one | after 40 confirmed answers | after 120 | |---|---|---|---| | laya, `laya.Learner` | 84.7% | 91.6% | **96.0%** | | Jev 1.14, confirmed answers written into its criteria | **89.5%** | 91.5% | 92.6% | Jev leads on day one (23 of 31 questions); they are level at 40; laya leads at 120 (12 wins, 7 losses, 12 ties). Jev cannot be taught, only prompted, and is a hosted API (364 ms a request from India). **What learning costs.** laya learns from 300 answers in 34 s on 8 CPU threads, with no GPU (0.72 s an answer, 6.4 GB of RAM; on a GPU 40 ms and 2 GB). Fine-tuning the classic encoder on the same 300 rows takes 89 s on a GPU with 9 GB and rewrites all 421M weights. **Learning from a stream, November 2026** (4B reader, held-out rows): | | laya | Jev 1.14 | |---|---|---| | banking77, 924 held out, after 4,928 rows | **87.5%**, ECE 0.028, 92.5% routed auto at 91.5% precision | 79.4% as shipped (ECE 0.078), 85.7% with examples | | typed-decisions, 2,000 decisions, after 1,200 rows | 73.7%, ECE **0.031** | 74.7%, ECE 0.047 (level) | **Across readers**, one byte-identical decision engine, 50,676 held-out records: 0.8B 76.5%, 4B 79.1%, 27B 81.1%, ECE 0.010 to 0.021. **Where it loses.** Zero-shot on generic public suites a large hosted model leads. As a prompt-injection gate on real traffic (ToxicChat, 1.8% attacks), Jev untaught catches 79.1% at 0.3% refused against 73.0% at 0.7% for a fitted head. The benchmarks further down are for the classic encoder checkpoints. Under the hood the new engine comes from [vegaml](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/vegaml), installed with laya. For the classic encoder, name it (`laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya")`) or pass `vegaml=False`. > **[Studio, from Embedding Space](https://studio.embedding.in)** builds the starting set for your questions and runs it for you. > **Cite this work.** M, N.; M, A. From Laya to Vega: Open Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities. *Preprints* **2026**, 2026110781. [https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1](https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1)
BibTeX ```bibtex @article{m2026laya_vega, title = {From Laya to Vega: Open Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities}, author = {M, N. and M, A.}, journal = {Preprints}, year = {2026}, pages = {2026110781}, doi = {10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1}, url = {https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202611.0781.v1} } ```
**Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine.** Typed decisions over 100+ languages in a single forward pass — 33 ms — trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD), with a router that picks the right checkpoint per request.
[![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/15d4Yv__KHeHjshVb-6PRTfqVllxih2S3?usp=sharing) [![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/laya.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/laya/) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-online-2ea44f)](https://nandhakishorm.github.io/laya/) [![Hugging Face Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Model-convaiinnovations%2Flaya-blue)](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya) [![Multilingual](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Model-laya--multilingual-blue)](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual) [![Hugging Face Space](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Space-laya--demo-orange)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/convaiinnovations/laya-demo) [![Dev.to Article](https://img.shields.io/badge/dev.to-Read%20Article-0A0A0A?logo=devdotto&logoColor=white)](https://dev.to/nandakishor_m_6cc0adfde9f/i-built-non-autoregressive-decision-models-a-year-ago-then-a-frontier-lab-called-it-a-18me) [![Buy Me A Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20A%20Coffee-nandakishorm-FFDD00?logo=buy-me-a-coffee&logoColor=black)](https://www.buymeacoffee.com/nandakishorm) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)
## Installation ```bash python -m pip install laya ``` With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), run `uv add laya` in a uv project or `uv pip install laya` in a virtual environment. Python 3.10 or newer. Optional extras: `laya[serve]` (HTTP server), `laya[mcp]` (MCP server), `laya[langchain]` (LangChain and LangGraph), `laya[llamaindex]` (LlamaIndex selectors), `laya[crewai]` (CrewAI routing), `laya[onnx]` (ONNX Runtime), `laya[fast]` (TileLang GPU fast path), `laya[structured]` (pydantic models in `decide`), `laya[vision]` (Pillow and torchvision, for `predict(image=...)` and `predict(video=...)`), `laya[audio]` (soundfile, to decode audio files). Step-by-step setup for each platform, CPU-only or GPU PyTorch builds, and troubleshooting are in [Installation details](#installation-details). For TypeScript / Node.js / browser, see [`laya-ts/`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/tree/main/laya-ts/). npm releases (`npm install laya-ts`) are published from this repository's `laya-ts-v*` release tags. **Long documents.** `laya-multilingual` reads up to 8,192 tokens with `max_len=8192`. Measured accuracy and time by document length, reproducible with [`research/scripts/bench_long_context.py`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/research/scripts/bench_long_context.py):

## Quickstart Since 0.5.0 `laya.Agent()` loads laya's new engine: a frozen 0.8B reader with a small physics engine on top, so every answer carries a conformal prediction set, an abstain flag, an out-of-distribution flag and a route decided without a threshold you had to guess at. Text, images, speech and 73k-token documents go through the same call. Python 3.10 or newer; details in [vega inside laya](#vega-inside-laya-agentvegamltrue). ```bash python -m pip install -U laya # 0.5.0 or newer: the new engine is the default ``` ```python import laya agent = laya.Agent() # the new engine with a 0.8B reader, the default since 0.5.0 # Switching the model underneath is one string. Every option keeps the same engine, questions and fields: # laya.Agent(vegaml="4b") # the Qwen3.5-4B reader from the same Hub repo # laya.Agent(vegaml="gemma-1b") # the gemma-3-1b-it reader, same repo # laya.Agent(vegaml="nandakishorm/vega-U") # any Hub repo id holding a vega-U checkpoint # laya.Agent(vegaml="./my-reader/") # a local dir from VegaAgent.attach(...), your own LLM ported in # laya.Agent(vegaml=True, backbone="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B") # name the reader weights explicitly, e.g. a mirror # Naming one of laya's own encoders loads it instead (or pass vegaml=False): # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya") # English, 33 ms on a T4 # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual") # 100+ languages, up to 8,192 tokens with max_len=8192 # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions") # fine-tuned for the typed-decisions workflows state = "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan." questions = { "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors", "other": "everything else"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?", "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]}, "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"}, } out = agent.predict(state, questions) ans = out["answers"]["department"] print(ans["choice"]) # billing print(ans["probabilities"]) # {"billing": 0.91, "technical": 0.04, "other": 0.05} print(ans["prediction_set"]) # ["billing"]: the options the answer could still be, at alpha 0.1 print(ans["abstain"]) # False: the engine is not refusing this one print(ans["unbound"]) # False: the state looks like something it has seen (reported, never routes) print(ans["route"]) # "auto"; "review" when the engine abstains or the set holds
